logicalBugs.explanation: Cancel retains the issue/PR title draft.

rootCause.explanation: The cancel handler only hides the title form. Reopening reuses its nonempty input rather than restoring the saved title.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Canceling an issue title edit restores the displayed saved title but retains the discarded draft in the editor.

sourceBugs.name: Canceled issue title draft reappears when editing again

reproductionPaths.expected: Reopening the title editor after Cancel should show the persisted issue title.
reproductionPaths.actual: On issue #2, replacing Clarify release ownership with FROZEN UNSAVED TITLE DRAFT and clicking Cancel restores the saved heading. Clicking Edit again shows FROZEN UNSAVED TITLE DRAFT in the textbox.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea and open an issue you can edit, such as eval/harbor-handbook issue #2.
Click Edit next to the issue title and replace it with a distinct temporary draft.
Click Cancel and verify the saved heading returns.
Click Edit again; the textbox still contains the canceled draft.

logicalBugs.explanation: Issue reference choices on the Tags tab do not save.

rootCause.explanation: initBranchSelector queries only the first .reference-list-menu (Branches) and binds its items. The separate Tags menu, including its Clear item, receives no update handler.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The issue sidebar offers an existing tag under Branch/Tag, but selecting it leaves the reference unset.

sourceBugs.name: Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting a listed tag should update the issue sidebar reference to that tag.
reproductionPaths.actual: On a seeded issue, selecting Tags > v1.0.0 closes the picker but the field still says No Branch/Tag Specified.
reproSteps: Sign in and open eval/harbor-handbook issue #2.
Open the No Branch/Tag Specified selector, choose Tags, and click v1.0.0.
Observe that the picker closes but the selector still reads No Branch/Tag Specified.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In an issue's Branch/Tag selector, 'Clear current reference' works from the Branches tab but does nothing from the Tags tab: the menu closes, no change is saved, and the previously selected branch stays on the issue. The Tags list has its own copy of the Clear item, and none of the Tags list's items have a click handler.

sourceBugs.name: Clear current reference from the Tags tab leaves the issue's branch set

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking 'Clear current reference' removes the issue's branch or tag reference whichever tab of the selector is open.
reproductionPaths.actual: With docs/release-owners saved on the issue, opening the selector's Tags tab and clicking 'Clear current reference' closed the menu without any request or timeline event; after refresh the branch was still set. The same item on the Branches tab cleared the reference. On the New Issue form the Tags tab's Clear item also left the chosen branch in place.
reproSteps: Open an issue and select a branch in the sidebar's Branch/Tag selector; refresh to confirm it's saved.
Open the selector, switch to the Tags tab, and click 'Clear current reference'.
Refresh and check whether the branch is still shown, and whether the timeline records a change.

relatedReference.name: Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the Tags list items get no click handler), but this entry is the 'Clear current reference' item on the Tags tab, which leaves an existing branch in place, not selecting a tag.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard state and ownership links discard active author/assignee filters.

rootCause.explanation: The dashboard builds $queryLink without poster or assignee, then uses it for ownership and Open/Closed links. $queryLinkWithFilter contains those fields but is only used by the filter and sort controls. Global and organization dashboards share this template.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The top-level Issues dashboard loses its selected assignee/author filter when Open or Closed is clicked, broadening the results to unrelated issues.

sourceBugs.name: Switching global Issues state drops the selected assignee or author filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Changing Open/Closed state should preserve the selected assignee and author and show only issues matching those filters in the newly selected state. A filtered count of zero Closed should open an empty filtered list.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Assignee=alex selected, the dashboard shows 2 Open / 0 Closed. Clicking 0 Closed removes assignee=alex from the destination URL and shows an unrelated closed issue, Publish the initial contributor guide; the counts become the unfiltered 3 Open / 1 Closed. Returning to Open also uses the broadened scope.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture account and open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues. Use the seeded alex-assigned open issues and unrelated closed issue, or create equivalent disposable records.
Choose alex from Assignee. Confirm assignee=alex is in the URL and the narrowed counts show 2 Open / 0 Closed.
Click 0 Closed. Observe that assignee=alex is absent from the new URL, and the unrelated closed issue appears instead of an empty alex-filtered list.
Click Open. Observe that the selected assignee remains cleared and the list/counts reflect the broadened scope.

guidance.deduplication: The existing Issues dashboard search-clears-assignee reference concerns submitting the keyword form. This reference requires clicking an Open/Closed state link. The existing organization-label state-switch reference concerns label selection, whose handler/template propagation is separate. Do not credit mere missing collapsed-filter indication or search-only filter loss here.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, clicking Open or Closed while an Assignee (or Author) is selected drops that filter, so the counts widen and unassigned issues appear.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues Open/Closed switch drops the selected Assignee filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Switching between Open and Closed keeps the selected Assignee and Author filters.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Closed and Open links omit the assignee parameter, so after switching the counts widen and issues not assigned to the selected user are listed.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create one issue assigned to yourself and one unassigned issue.
On the organization's Issues page, choose yourself in the Assignee filter; only the assigned issue is listed.
Click Closed, then Open.
Check whether the Assignee filter is still applied and whether the unassigned issue is now listed.

relatedReference.name: Switching global Issues state drops the selected assignee or author filter
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard Open/Closed links, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the global Issues page, after selecting an Assignee filter, clicking an ownership link such as Created by you drops the assignee, so issues assigned to other users appear and the counts change.

sourceBugs.name: Global Issues ownership links drop the selected Assignee filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Switching between ownership views keeps the selected Assignee filter applied.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a search, an Author and an Assignee applied (No results), clicking Created by you opened a URL without the assignee parameter, and an issue assigned to a different user appeared with changed Open and Closed counts.
reproSteps: Open the global Issues page, search for a term and select an Author and an Assignee so the results are narrowed.
Click Created by you (or another ownership link) in the sidebar.
Check whether the Assignee filter is still applied in the URL and results.

relatedReference.distinction: Same ownership links on the global Issues page. That entry drops the label filter; this entry drops the Assignee filter.

guidance.scope: Global Issues ownership links (Created by you, Your repositories, Assigned to you and similar) dropping a selected Assignee filter.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, with an Assignee filter applied, clicking the already-selected 'In your repositories' sidebar entry removes the assignee from the URL, so unassigned issues reappear. The sort order is kept.

sourceBugs.name: Reselecting the active In your repositories entry drops the organization Issues Assignee filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking the sidebar entry that is already selected keeps the Assignee filter, so only issues assigned to that user stay listed.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Assignee set to one user (one issue listed) and Oldest sorting, clicking the active 'In your repositories' entry reloaded without the assignee parameter and listed all three open issues, including the two unassigned ones.
reproSteps: Open an organization's Issues page with several open issues, only one assigned to a given user.
Choose that user in the Assignee filter, so only their issue is listed, and choose Sort > Oldest.
Click the already-active 'In your repositories' entry in the sidebar.
Check whether the Assignee filter is still applied in the URL and results.

relatedReference.distinction: Same kind of ownership-link navigation dropping the Assignee filter. That entry is the global Issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page and reselecting the already-active entry.

guidance.scope: Organization Issues: clicking the sidebar ownership entry (including the already-active one) drops an explicitly selected Assignee filter.

logicalBugs.explanation: An empty keyword match set produces an unfiltered tracked-time aggregate.

rootCause.explanation: The list passes an empty IssueIDs slice for zero keyword matches. The aggregate delegates to IssuesOptions conditions, which add an issue.id restriction only when len(IssueIDs)>0, conflating no matches with no restriction.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When issue text search matches no rows, the displayed tracked-time total includes time from issues excluded by the search.

sourceBugs.name: Issue-list tracked time includes issues excluded by text search

reproductionPaths.expected: When text search returns no issues, show zero tracked time or hide the tracked-time summary. Do not include time belonging to excluded issues.
reproductionPaths.actual: A nonmatching search shows No results but retains a tracked-time total of 1 hour 30 minutes; the tooltip says that the total follows the list filters.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval in a writable repository with time tracking enabled. Through the UI, create a disposable issue and record 1 hour 30 minutes using Time Tracker > Add Time.
Open the repository Issues list and confirm that the tracked-time summary includes the recorded duration.
Search for a unique token matching none of the issue titles or bodies.
Confirm the issue list shows No results while the tracked-time summary still includes the excluded issue’s 1 hour 30 minutes. Inspect its filter-based tooltip.

guidance.matchScope: Only the zero-keyword-match aggregate failure. Searches with a nonempty matched-ID set apply the restriction normally; unrelated stopped-timer or lost-filter reports do not match.

logicalBugs.explanation: Activity dates treat the year-0001 zero instant as absent.

rootCause.explanation: Deadline comments serialize a date string; DateUtils.ParseLegacy reconstructs midnight as a Go time.Time. AbsoluteLong treats the Go zero instant as missing, so accepted 0001-01-01 dates become a dash in the timeline.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The issue sidebar correctly saves and shows January 1, 0001, but its activity history replaces that date with a dash. Changing the date also records the previous value as a dash.

sourceBugs.name: Issue due-date history renders January 1, 0001 as missing

reproductionPaths.expected: A due date accepted and displayed in the sidebar should be identified consistently in the activity history, including the previous date when it is changed.
reproductionPaths.actual: The sidebar shows January 1, 1, while the timeline says “eval added the due date -”. Changing the due date to December 31, 9999 produces “eval modified the due date from - to December 31, 9999”. The red overdue styling and sidebar date are correct.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval on the seeded Gitea fixture with UTC date parsing. Create a disposable issue in a writable repository.
In the Due Date control, enter January 1, 0001 (0001-01-01) and save using the adjacent plus control. Confirm the sidebar displays January 1, 1.
Inspect the activity history: its added-date entry shows a dash instead of January 1, 0001.
Edit the due date to December 31, 9999 (9999-12-31), save, and confirm the sidebar shows that date.
Inspect the new history entry: the previous due date is shown as a dash, while the replacement date is displayed correctly.

guidance.scope: January 1, 0001 under date parsing that yields the UTC zero instant. Do not generalize to every date in year 0001 or ordinary due dates. Saving the date and the sidebar’s overdue styling work correctly; the accepted defect is history display only.

logicalBugs.explanation: The participant count always uses the plural noun.

rootCause.explanation: The English translation has a single %d Participants string and the sidebar passes the count to it without singular selection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: An issue with one participant displays the plural label “1 Participants” in its sidebar.

sourceBugs.name: Issue sidebar says 1 Participants

reproductionPaths.expected: One participant should use the singular label “1 Participant.”
reproductionPaths.actual: An issue with one participant displays the plural label “1 Participants” in its sidebar.
reproSteps: Open an issue with one participant in the seeded repository.
Inspect the Participants label in the right sidebar.

logicalBugs.explanation: A rejected Close with Comment hides a successfully persisted comment.

rootCause.explanation: CreateComment persists the comment before its deferred status change. If dependency validation rejects closure, the defer returns a JSON error before the redirect that would show the new comment and reset the editor. Retrying repeats comment creation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Close with Comment posts the comment before dependency rejection, but leaves it invisible and retains its draft; retrying posts an identical duplicate.

sourceBugs.name: Blocked Close with Comment silently saves the comment, keeps the draft, and duplicates it on retry

reproductionPaths.expected: When a dependency blocks closure after the comment has been posted, show the posted comment, clear the submitted draft, and display the dependency error while leaving the issue Open. The UI must reflect the persisted comment so retrying does not unknowingly duplicate it.
reproductionPaths.actual: Each Close with Comment attempt shows only the blocking-dependency error. The editor retains the draft and the timeline/count stay unchanged. After two attempts, reload reveals two identical saved comments while the issue remains Open.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. Create two open disposable issues A and B and configure A as blocked by B through the dependency UI.
Open A, type a unique sentinel in its comment editor, and click Close with Comment.
Observe the dependency error, retained draft, and no displayed new comment. Click Close with Comment again without changing the draft.
Reload. Confirm A is still Open and two identical sentinel comments are present.

guidance.matchScope: Credit hidden successful posting combined with retained draft or duplicate retry after rejected Close with Comment. Do not match a claim that any comment persistence during blocked closure is inherently wrong.

logicalBugs.explanation: Attachment-only comments cannot use the Comment button.

rootCause.explanation: syncUiState disables Comment whenever editor text is empty, ignoring completed uploaded files, although the server explicitly accepts empty content with attachments.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After a PNG upload finishes, the issue editor still disables Comment when its text is empty, preventing supported attachment-only submission without changing issue state.

sourceBugs.name: Completed attachment-only upload leaves the issue Comment button disabled

reproductionPaths.expected: A completed attachment should enable Comment even with empty text, allowing an attachment-only comment while leaving the issue open. Buttons should remain disabled while an upload is still in progress.
reproductionPaths.actual: A completed PNG preview with Remove file and Copy link appears, but the separate Comment button stays visibly grey and clicking it does nothing. Adding text enables Comment; removing the text disables it again. Close Issue posts that same attachment with empty text and closes the issue; reload confirms the attachment-only comment persisted.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open an existing issue in an initialized repository with an empty comment editor.
Upload a valid PNG through the normal attachment chooser. Wait for completion: the image preview, Remove file and Copy link are visible.
Leave comment text empty and click the physical Comment button. Observe that it stays grey and no comment is posted.
Enter text and observe Comment becomes enabled; clear the text and observe it becomes disabled despite the completed attachment.

As a terminal control, click Close Issue: the attachment-only comment posts and the issue closes. Reload to confirm the saved attachment, then reopen the issue. This control demonstrates supported attachment-only content; closing is not the expected standalone Comment behavior.

logicalBugs.explanation: Clicking an active Open/Closed state selects all states.

rootCause.explanation: The shared openclose template deliberately selects $allStatesLink when the clicked state equals .State. The Open label does not indicate that its destination becomes state=all.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Clicking the Open count from the unfiltered issue list navigates to state=all and includes a closed issue.

sourceBugs.name: Initial Open issues control includes closed issues

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking Open should display only open issues.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking the Open count from the unfiltered issue list navigates to state=all and includes a closed issue.
reproSteps: Open the seeded repository Issues list with no state filter and note the separate Open and Closed counts.
Click Open and observe state=all in the URL and a closed issue in the resulting list.

logicalBugs.explanation: Deleting a comment does not refresh the issue header comment count.

rootCause.explanation: The delete handler removes the timeline DOM node and updates review counters, but never changes the issue header count, leaving the original server-rendered value until navigation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After deleting the only comment, its card disappears but the issue header continues to say “1 comment” until refresh.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting an issue comment leaves its count stale

reproductionPaths.expected: The issue header should update to 0 comments when the comment is deleted.
reproductionPaths.actual: After deleting the only comment, its card disappears but the issue header continues to say “1 comment” until refresh.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue and add one comment.
Delete the comment from its action menu.
Observe that the card disappears but the header still says 1 comment; refresh to see 0 comments.

logicalBugs.explanation: Issue dashboards admit repositories without usable issue access.

rootCause.explanation: SearchRepositoryCondition admits owned organization repositories and checks actor access with unit.TypeInvalid. The Issues UnitType does not constrain those repositories; dashboard search then loads their issues without per-issue unit authorization. Both disabled trackers and teams with Issues No Access pass this same repository selection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Disabling a repository issue tracker leaves its open issue in organization and global dashboard results/counts, with an actionable title leading to 404.

sourceBugs.name: Issue dashboards list and count issues from repositories with the issue tracker disabled

reproductionPaths.expected: Organization and global Issues dashboards should exclude issues from repositories whose issue tracker is disabled, including their contribution to displayed counts. Disabling the feature should not leave an actionable result pointing at an unavailable issue.
reproductionPaths.actual: After disabling the tracker, the repository has no Issues tab, but the organization dashboard and global keyword-filtered dashboard still show the issue and 1 Open. Clicking its visible title opens 404 Not Found while the same administrator retains repository access.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval with administration access. Create a disposable organization and initialized repository, then create an open issue with a distinctive title and confirm its detail page opens.
In repository Settings, disable Enable Repository Issue Tracker and save. Confirm the Issues tab is no longer present.
Use the organization Issues dashboard. Observe that the disabled repository issue remains listed and counted as open.
Click the visible issue title and observe 404 Not Found.

Open the global Issues dashboard and search the distinctive title. Observe that the same issue remains listed and contributes to the open count. Repository access is unchanged; the defect is stale dashboard membership/counts, not the disabled detail route itself.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A team member whose team has Code Read but Issues No Access on a private organization repository can't open that repository's issues, but the organization (and team) Issues dashboards still list them with title, repository and number, author and Open count.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues dashboard shows issues from repositories where the team has Issues No Access

reproductionPaths.expected: Issues from a repository where the user's team has Issues No Access are left out of the organization and team Issues dashboards and their counts, as they are from the user's personal Issues dashboard.
reproductionPaths.actual: The organization Issues dashboard listed the private issue's title, repo#number and author and counted it as 1 Open. The repository had no Issues tab for the user, and opening the issue, including from the dashboard link, returned 404. Switching the team to Issues Read made the issue open normally.
reproSteps: In an organization, create a private repository with an open issue.
Create a team for specific repositories with that repository, Code Read and Issues No Access, and add a member.
As that member, confirm the repository has no Issues tab and the issue URL returns 404.
As that member, open the organization's Issues dashboard and check whether the issue is listed and counted.

guidance.scope: Organization or team Issues dashboards listing issues (titles, numbers, authors or counts) from repositories where the user's team has Issues No Access. A distinct bug from issue trackers being disabled for a repository.

logicalBugs.explanation: Keyword search indexes the legacy assignee field instead of actual assignees.

rootCause.explanation: Indexer conversion copies Issue.AssigneeID, a nonpersisted legacy field, instead of Issue.Assignees. Specific, self and any-assignee filters therefore query incorrect indexed data. Non-keyword database filtering uses issue_assignees and succeeds.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Exact-title search hides a matching issue in Assigned to you while Created by you returns it.

sourceBugs.name: Assigned-to-you exact search omits a matching issue

reproductionPaths.expected: An open issue assigned to the signed-in user remains visible when searching for its exact title.
reproductionPaths.actual: Assigned to you returns no results; the same query under Created by you returns the issue.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create an issue titled mo-issues-assigned-search-7c91f0 in eval/harbor-handbook.
Assign the issue to eval. Open global Issues > Assigned to you and confirm it is listed.
Search for mo-issues-assigned-search-7c91f0 with Exact selected; observe zero results.
Keep the query and switch to Created by you; the issue appears. Return to Assigned to you; it is absent.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a repository's issue list, searching a fresh issue's title lists it, but adding the Assignee filter for its visible assignee shows No results.

sourceBugs.name: Repository issue search with an Assignee filter omits a matching assigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: The assigned, matching issue stays listed when filtering by its assignee.
reproductionPaths.actual: No results is displayed, with no other filters applied.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a disposable issue with a unique title, assigned to yourself.
In the repository Issues list, search its unique title and confirm it is listed.
Open Assignee and select yourself; observe No results.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, 'Assigned to you' with a search query returns no results even though an issue assigned to the signed-in user matches it; the same query under 'In your repositories' lists the issue.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues 'Assigned to you' search omits a matching assigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: An issue assigned to the signed-in user stays in the organization's 'Assigned to you' list when a search query matches it.
reproductionPaths.actual: The organization's 'In your repositories' list showed 'ORG Alpha search needle' for a Words search of 'needle Alpha'. Switching to 'Assigned to you' with the same query showed 0 and No results, while the issue's Assignees still listed the user.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
Open the organization's Issues page and search for words from the issue's title.
Confirm the issue appears under 'In your repositories', then switch to 'Assigned to you' with the same query.

relatedReference.name: Assigned-to-you exact search omits a matching issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store assignees), but this entry is the organization Issues page rather than the global Issues dashboard.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, choosing a user in the Assignee filter while a text search is active shows No results, even though an issue assigned to that user matches the search. The search index doesn't store current assignees.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues Assignee filter with a search hides a matching assigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: An issue assigned to the selected user stays listed when the organization Issues page is filtered by that Assignee and a matching search.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the search 'Alpha' listing 'OR-4821 Alpha searchable' (assigned to eval) on the organization Issues page, choosing eval in the Assignee filter showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed, while 'In your repositories' still counted 1.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
On the organization's Issues page, search for a word from its title and confirm it's listed.
Choose yourself in the Assignee filter.
Check whether the issue is still listed.

relatedReference.name: Organization Issues 'Assigned to you' search omits a matching assigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store current assignees) on the same page, but that entry is the 'Assigned to you' tab; this entry is the Assignee dropdown filter.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a repository's Issues list, choosing Type → Assigned to you while a text search is active shows No results, even though an issue assigned to you matches the search. The search index doesn't store current assignees.

sourceBugs.name: Repository Issues 'Assigned to you' with a search hides a matching assigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: An issue assigned to you that matches the search stays listed when the repository Issues list is filtered to Assigned to you.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a search matching an issue assigned to the signed-in user, choosing Assigned to you showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed. Without the search, or with All issues and the same search, the issue was listed.
reproSteps: In a repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
On the repository's Issues list, search for a word from its title and confirm it's listed.
Choose Type → Assigned to you.
Check whether the issue is still listed.

relatedReference.name: Repository issue search with an Assignee filter omits a matching assigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store current assignees) on the same page, but that entry is the Assignee dropdown; this entry is the Type → Assigned to you control.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Combining a matching text search with Assignee → Assigned to anybody on a repository Issues list hides assigned issues and shows zero Open and Closed counts. Bulk assignment succeeds; the search index uses an unpopulated legacy assignee field.

sourceBugs.name: Repository issue search with Assigned to anybody hides matching assigned issues

reproductionPaths.expected: Matching issues with at least one assignee remain listed when text search is combined with Assigned to anybody.
reproductionPaths.actual: The search alone lists the assigned issue, and Assigned to anybody without search lists it. Combining the two shows No results and zero counts despite the assignment remaining visible on the issue. The failure persists after reload and also affects assignments made from the issue sidebar.
reproSteps: Create two disposable issues sharing a unique searchable title prefix, with no milestone.
Assign one issue to a contributor, using its sidebar or the list bulk-assignment action.
Search for their shared title prefix on the repository Issues list and confirm both issues appear.
Choose Assignee → Assigned to anybody and observe the assigned issue disappears, with No results and zero Open/Closed counts.
Remove the text search while retaining Assigned to anybody and confirm the assigned issue appears.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing entry covers selecting a specific named user in the repository Assignee dropdown. This entry covers its Assigned to anybody option. Type → Assigned to you and organization/global dashboards have separate related references.

guidance.scope: Require a matching text search together with Assigned to anybody. Assignment itself succeeds, and filtering without a keyword works. Do not infer that bulk assignment failed or that every dashboard/API variant was browser-tested.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the global Issues page, with a text search active, choosing a user in the Assignee filter shows No results even though an issue assigned to that user matches the search.

sourceBugs.name: Global Issues Assignee filter with a search hides a matching assigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting the assignee keeps the matching issue assigned to that user in the results.
reproductionPaths.actual: After searching for a word in a newly created issue's title under Created by you, choosing its assignee in the Assignee filter removed the issue and showed No results.
reproSteps: Create an issue and assign it to yourself.
Open the global Issues page, select Created by you and search for a word from the issue's title.
Open the Assignee filter and choose yourself.
Check whether the issue is still listed.

relatedReference.distinction: Same search plus Assignee filter omission. That entry is an organization's Issues page; this entry is the global Issues page.

otherRelatedReference.distinction: Same omission on a repository's issue list.

guidance.scope: Global Issues page: an active text search combined with an Assignee filter hides an issue assigned to that user.

logicalBugs.explanation: Bulk status changes swallow dependency rejection.

rootCause.explanation: The server returns HTTP 412 for blocked closure. updateIssuesMeta awaits POST without checking response.ok, and the caller reloads as though the change succeeded, losing selection and error details.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The issue-list bulk Close action silently skips issues with open dependencies. It deselects the issue and leaves it Open without explaining why, while the individual Close Issue action reports the blocking dependency.

sourceBugs.name: Bulk closing a blocked issue silently fails without feedback

reproductionPaths.expected: Bulk Close should show which issues could not close and explain their open dependencies, consistent with the individual issue action.
reproductionPaths.actual: For a single selected blocked issue, bulk Close returns to the same list with 1 Open and 0 Closed, deselects the issue, and displays no error, toast, or explanation. Direct Close Issue on the same issue displays the blocking-dependencies error. An unblocked issue closes successfully through bulk Close.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and create two open issues A and B, with A depending on B. Verified with /admin/harbor-handbook/issues/12 depending on open #5, which has no dependencies.
Open A and click Close Issue; confirm the dependency error and that A remains Open.
Open /admin/harbor-handbook/issues and search for A's title (QA acyclic blocked bulk close).
Select A's checkbox and choose the bulk Close action.
Observe the checkbox is deselected, the issue remains Open, and no failure reason is shown.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dependency creation checks only direct reverse edges.

rootCause.explanation: CreateIssueDependency checks issueDepExists(dep.ID, issue.ID) rather than transitive reachability. Three or more edges can form a cycle that blocks every close operation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Dependency validation prevents direct two-issue cycles but accepts transitive cycles. Three open issues can each become blocked by another issue in the cycle, leaving all unable to close until a dependency is removed.

sourceBugs.name: Three-issue dependency cycles are accepted and block closing every issue

reproductionPaths.expected: Adding a dependency that would create a cycle of any length should be rejected, as direct mutual dependencies already are.
reproductionPaths.actual: A depends on B, B depends on C, and C depends on A are all accepted and persist after reload. Close Issue fails for each with 'You need to close all issues blocking this issue before you can close it.' The direct C depends on B alternative is correctly rejected.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin. In /admin/harbor-handbook/issues create three open issues A, B, and C (verified using #7, #8, #9).
On A, use Add dependency, search for B, select it, and add it so A depends on B.
On B, add C as a dependency.
On C, add A as a dependency; observe that it is accepted. Reload and confirm C still depends on A.
Open each of A, B, and C and click Close Issue. Each remains Open with the blocking-dependencies error.
As a control, remove C's dependency on A and try adding B to C; the direct two-issue cycle is rejected. Adding A back is accepted again.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dependency-rejected closure changes timer state.

rootCause.explanation: CloseIssue calls FinishIssueStopwatchIfPossible even on ErrDependenciesLeft. The rejected action can finish/log the stopwatch, while the error response suppresses page refresh, leaving issue-sidebar timer controls stale. These are two observations of the same failed-close side effect.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Closing an issue blocked by an open dependency stops its timer, but the Time Tracker menu continues to offer Stop timer and Discard timer until the page is reloaded.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected issue closure leaves the time tracker showing a stopped timer as running
Rejected close of an issue with an open blocking dependency stops its running timer

reproductionPaths.expected: After a rejected closure stops the active timer, the Time Tracker menu should reflect the stopped state and offer Start timer without requiring a manual reload.
reproductionPaths.actual: The dependency error appears and the issue remains Open. The Time Tracker menu still shows Stop timer and Discard timer as if the timer were running. After reload, the same menu offers Start timer and the timeline shows the elapsed time logged by the rejected closure.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository. Create an open issue named QA stale timer display and add the open issue Clarify release ownership (#2) as a dependency.
On QA stale timer display, open Time Tracker and choose Start timer.
Wait a few seconds, then click Close Issue.
Observe the dependency error and the issue remaining Open. Without reloading, open Time Tracker and observe Stop timer and Discard timer still offered. Wait five seconds and check again.
Reload the page and open Time Tracker. Observe Start timer replacing Stop timer and Discard timer, and elapsed time logged in the timeline.

guidance.relatedExistingReference: codex-30m-gitea-3 covers the exact same issue-detail workflow but the stale controls before reload. This reference covers persisted timer completion despite rejected closure, demonstrable after reload without any stale-controls allegation. Preserve both symptom scopes; do not require a stale display to match this reference.

logicalBugs.explanation: Quote Reply programmatically changes text without notifying button state.

rootCause.explanation: tryOnQuoteReply uses ComboMarkdownEditor.value(v). The textarea setter changes value without dispatching EventEditorContentChanged, while comment button state listens to that event and upload events. Typing finally resynchronizes it.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On issue #1, Quote Reply puts a non-empty quote in the comment box. The Comment button stays disabled and the close button still says "Close Issue". Pressing Space and then Backspace leaves the same text, but then Comment becomes enabled and the close button changes to "Close with Comment".

sourceBugs.name: Quote Reply fills the comment box but leaves Comment disabled until the user types

reproductionPaths.expected: After Quote Reply inserts a non-empty draft, Comment should be enabled and the close button should say "Close with Comment". This is what happens with the same text after a keyboard edit.
reproductionPaths.actual: Right after Quote Reply, the box shows "> I will draft the first-week checklist and link the access request instructions." but Comment is greyed out and the close button still says "Close Issue". After pressing Space and then Backspace, the text is unchanged, Comment is enabled and the close button says "Close with Comment".
reproSteps: Use the supplied saved signed-in session for the fixture admin account (eval).
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/1 with the comment box empty.
Open the three-dot menu on alex's comment and choose Quote Reply.
Check that the box contains the quoted text, Comment is disabled and the close button says "Close Issue".
Press Space, then Backspace. Comment is now enabled and the close button says "Close with Comment".

logicalBugs.explanation: Negative time validation exposes a binding error.

rootCause.explanation: Hours is constrained with binding Range(0,1000). AddTimeManually returns the generic form error via GetErrMsg before reaching its readable duration validation, exposing the untranslated range binding feedback.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Submitting -1 hours and 0 minutes in Manually Add Time correctly rejects the duration but displays untranslated RangeError feedback.

sourceBugs.name: Negative manual time exposes raw range-validation feedback

reproductionPaths.expected: Reject the negative duration with a readable validation message explaining how to correct the input.
reproductionPaths.actual: The error feedback includes the internal text RangeError: Range instead of an explanation of the allowed duration. The dialog stays open with the entered values and no time is recorded; those rejection behaviors are expected.
reproSteps: Sign in as a contributor with repository write access in the time-tracking-enabled fixture. Open eval/harbor-handbook > Issues and create a disposable issue.
Open the issue's Time Tracker menu and choose Add Time.
Enter -1 in Hours and 0 in Minutes, then submit Add Time.
Observe the untranslated RangeError: Range feedback. The negative duration is correctly rejected and the dialog remains available for correction.

logicalBugs.explanation: New task lists inserted by inline edits have no input handlers.

rootCause.explanation: saveAndRefresh replaces renderContent.innerHTML but only attaches reference popups; it never calls initMarkupTasklist on the replacement markup. Page initialization attaches those handlers after reload.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After adding task-list items to an issue body with inline Edit, clicking a new unchecked box does nothing; after a reload the same click checks and saves it.

sourceBugs.name: Task checkboxes added by inline issue edit are inert until reload

reproductionPaths.expected: Task checkboxes rendered after saving an inline edit should toggle and save, as they do after a reload.
reproductionPaths.actual: The checkbox stays unchecked and nothing is saved until the page is reloaded.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a disposable issue with a plain body.
Use the body's menu > Edit, replace the body with '- [ ] First task' and '- [x] Done task', and Save.
Without reloading, click the unchecked First task box; observe nothing changes.
Reload and click it again; observe it checks and persists.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard keyword search fails to submit selected user filters.

rootCause.explanation: The shared dashboard search form submits only type, sort, state and search-combo fields. It has no poster or assignee hidden input, so submitting a keyword discards those filters on both global and organization dashboards.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Submitting search on the top-level Issues dashboard drops the selected assignee filter and displays a matching unassigned issue that was excluded before the search.

sourceBugs.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue

reproductionPaths.expected: Search should retain the selected assignee and return only matching issues assigned to that user.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Assignee=eval selected, the dashboard URL contains assignee=eval and excludes the unassigned fixture. Submitting a keyword shared by the assigned and unassigned fixtures removes assignee=eval and shows both issues. The unassigned result remains visible after waiting for the search to settle.
reproSteps: Sign in as the Gitea fixture account eval. Use fresh disposable records and a unique shared title token.
Create two open issues in a writable repository, both containing the shared title token. Assign one to eval and leave the other unassigned.
Open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues, keep the Open state, and select eval through its Assignee control.
Confirm the URL contains assignee=eval and the unassigned issue is excluded from the narrowed list.
Enter the shared token into the dashboard search and press Enter.
Observe that assignee=eval disappears from the URL and the results include both fixtures, including the unassigned issue. Wait at least five seconds to confirm the broadened result remains.

guidance.scope: Accept the independently reproduced assignee-search failure on the Issues dashboard. Author, label, and Open/Closed variants are not required for matching this reference.
guidance.deduplication: The Issues and Pull Requests reports share an implementation defect but affect separate eval product areas and record types. Keep separate grading slots under the existing grading contract. The accepted Assigned-to-you exact-search omission describes a different result and trigger.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the top-level Issues dashboard, submitting a text search clears the selected Author filter, so issues by other authors appear in the results.

sourceBugs.name: Global Issues search drops the selected Author filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Submitting a search on the Issues dashboard keeps the selected Author filter.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Author set to alex and a search showing no results, changing the search text and pressing Enter cleared the Author filter, and issues authored by eval appeared.
reproSteps: Open the top-level Issues dashboard.
Choose an Author in the Author filter.
Type a search term matching another user's issue and press Enter.
Check whether the Author filter is still selected and whether other authors' issues appear.

relatedReference.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same Issues dashboard search form. That entry is the Assignee filter being dropped; this entry is the Author filter being dropped.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Author is selected drops the Author filter, so issues by other authors that match the search appear.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues search drops the selected Author filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Text search combines with the selected Author filter, so issues by other authors stay excluded.
reproductionPaths.actual: The search navigates to a URL without the poster parameter, and an issue by a different author that matches the search is listed.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue whose title contains a unique word, authored by yourself.
On the organization's Issues page, choose a different user in the Author filter; the issue isn't listed.
Search for the unique word and submit.
Check whether your own issue is now listed and whether the Author filter is still applied.

relatedReference.name: Global Issues search drops the selected Author filter
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard search form, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Assignee is selected drops the Assignee filter, so unassigned issues that match the search appear.

sourceBugs.name: Organization Issues search drops the selected Assignee filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Text search combines with the selected Assignee filter, so issues not assigned to that user stay excluded.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Assignee set to the signed-in user, submitting a search removed the filter and listed an unassigned matching issue.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create one issue assigned to yourself and one unassigned issue with a shared title word.
On the organization's Issues page, choose yourself in the Assignee filter.
Search for the shared word and submit.
Check whether the unassigned issue is now listed.

relatedReference.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard search form, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard user filters have no visible selected indicator.

rootCause.explanation: filter_item_user_fetch records the selected username only in a data attribute used inside the remote dropdown. The closed control always renders the same title and classes, regardless of selection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The top-level Issues dashboard does not visibly distinguish Assignee=eval from no explicit assignee filter while the dropdown is closed.

sourceBugs.name: Issues dashboard does not visibly indicate the active assignee outside the dropdown

reproductionPaths.expected: The collapsed filter control or another visible indicator should identify the active assignee, so the current result scope is apparent without opening the dropdown or reading the URL.
reproductionPaths.actual: With assignee=eval active, the closed control still displays only Assignee with the same styling as the unfiltered control and no selected-name chip, avatar, or active badge. Reopening the dropdown reveals eval in its input. Without a keyword, assigned records are correctly retained and unassigned records excluded; the missing feedback is a visual-state defect, separate from search dropping the filter.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture account eval and open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues with In your repositories and Open selected. Use disposable assigned and unassigned records to compare the unfiltered and filtered results.
Open Assignee, select eval, and close the dropdown. Confirm assignee=eval is in the URL and unassigned records are excluded.
Inspect the collapsed results view. The control still reads only Assignee and has no selected username, avatar, chip, or active styling to distinguish it from the unfiltered state.
Reopen Assignee and observe eval in its input; close it and observe that the selection is no longer visibly identified.

Repeat the display comparison with a keyword q and assignee=eval both present in the /issues URL. The collapsed control still reads only Assignee. This step checks selection feedback rather than the correctness of exact-search results.

guidance.scope: Missing indication in the collapsed results view; do not claim the selection is invisible inside the opened menu. A generic label after search has genuinely cleared the filter is not this defect.
guidance.deduplication: Separate Issues and Pull Requests product-area references for their independently observed collapsed controls. Neither matches the accepted assignee-search broadening references, where the filter itself is removed.

logicalBugs.explanation: Farthest-due sorting treats an undated milestone as an earlier deadline.

rootCause.explanation: The DESC CASE handles NULL milestone deadlines but not 0. The next branch selects milestone.deadline_unix=0 over a positive issue deadline; the ASC implementation explicitly handles zero and works.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When issues with different due dates are assigned to an existing milestone with no due date, Farthest due date sorts them by creation order instead of their issue dates. Without the milestone, or with Nearest due date, the issue-date order is correct.

sourceBugs.name: Farthest due sort uses an undated milestone as the issue date
Farthest due date sort drops an issue below earlier dates when it is in a milestone with no due date

reproductionPaths.expected: For Farthest due date sorting, an assigned milestone with no due date should not override the issue due dates. The issues should remain ordered by their actual due dates; a dated milestone can still provide the milestone deadline.
reproductionPaths.actual: With no milestone assigned, issues #2 (February 1, 2027), #4 (January 1, 2027), and #1 (December 1, 2026) sort correctly as #2, #4, #1. After assigning all three to the existing undated “Handbook 1.1” milestone, Farthest due date returns #4, #2, #1 and keeps that order after reload and direct navigation to the same correctly sorted URL. Nearest due date remains correct.
reproSteps: In the seeded repository, use open issues #1, #2, and #4 with due dates December 1, 2026; February 1, 2027; and January 1, 2027 respectively. Their creation order differs from descending due-date order.
With no milestone assigned, open Sort and choose Farthest due date from the actual menu. Confirm the URL uses sort=farduedate and the dated issues are ordered #2, #4, #1.
Assign the three issues to the existing “Handbook 1.1” milestone, whose due date is empty. Confirm the milestone has no due date.
Again choose Farthest due date from the actual Sort menu and confirm the URL uses sort=farduedate. The list is now #4, #2, #1, which does not follow the February, January, December issue dates.

Reload the correctly sorted URL, then navigate directly to that same URL. Confirm the wrong #4, #2, #1 order persists. As a contrast, choose Nearest due date and confirm its dated issue order remains correct.

guidance.requiredCondition: At least two issues have positive, distinct due dates, are assigned to the same existing milestone with an empty due date, and their creation order differs from descending due-date order.
guidance.negativeControl: A fresh no-milestone case correctly sorts #2 February, #4 January, #1 December; it does not include the required milestone condition and does not disprove this narrower finding.

relatedReference.name: Farthest due sort uses an undated milestone as the issue date
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause, but here only one issue is in the undated milestone, so it drops below issues with earlier due dates; the related entry has all issues in that milestone falling back to creation order.

logicalBugs.explanation: Successful fetch-action forms remain loading if navigation is canceled.

rootCause.explanation: On HTTP 200 fetchActionDoRequest ignores dirty state only for the submitted form, calls reload/redirect, then returns before removing is-loading. A different dirty form can cancel navigation; the successful dialog remains locked because later submits return while is-loading is set.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Saving a time estimate (or manual time) succeeds on the server, but the page then reloads to show it. When any other form on the issue page counts as unsaved, the browser asks whether to leave the page; choosing to stay leaves the dialog spinning forever and every later Save does nothing. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog is enough to make its form count as unsaved, so the warning can appear with no real unsaved work.

sourceBugs.name: Time tracker dialog freezes on its spinner after a successful save when the page has other unsaved input

reproductionPaths.expected: After a successful save the dialog either closes and shows the new value, or, if the reload is cancelled, returns to a usable state. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog does not leave unsaved changes behind.
reproductionPaths.actual: On an issue where Add time manually was opened and cancelled (or the comment box has a draft), saving an estimate of 90m returns success and stores 1h 30m, then the browser shows a leave-page warning. Choosing to stay leaves the Set estimated time dialog on a loading spinner indefinitely; clicking Save again sends no request and no error appears. After a reload the sidebar shows Estimate: 1h 30m.
reproSteps: Open an issue in a repository with time tracking enabled.
In the sidebar, open Add time manually, type a value such as 1h, and click Cancel.
Open Set estimated time, enter 90m, and click Save.
When the browser asks whether to leave the page, choose to stay.
Observe the dialog stays on its loading spinner and clicking Save again does nothing. Reload and observe the estimate was saved.

logicalBugs.explanation: Deleted issues remain in keyword search counts and pagination.

rootCause.explanation: DeleteIssue emits a notification, but indexerNotifier inherits the no-op DeleteIssue from NullNotifier rather than deleting the indexed document. Indexed counts and slots outlive the database issue; row loading drops the deleted row.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Deleting an issue never removes it from the issue search index, so keyword searches on the global Issues dashboard keep counting the deleted issue in the Open/Closed and sidebar totals and reserve page slots for it, while the list itself shows only the issues that still exist.

sourceBugs.name: Deleted issues keep counting in global issue search totals and pagination

reproductionPaths.expected: After an issue is deleted, keyword searches that matched it no longer count it, and their pages are filled with existing issues, as the repository's own issue list does.
reproductionPaths.actual: With three issues matching a keyword, the global Issues dashboard shows 3 Open and 3 rows. After deleting one (its page returns 404), the same search still shows 3 Open and 'In your repositories 3' but lists only 2 issues, including after waiting and reloading. The repository issue list with the same keyword shows 2 Open. With more deletions, pages come back short and trailing pages can be empty.
reproSteps: Create three issues whose titles contain the same distinctive word.
On the global Issues dashboard, search for that word and note 3 Open with 3 rows.
Open one of the issues and delete it from the sidebar.
Repeat the global search: observe it still says 3 Open while listing 2 issues.
Run the same search on the repository's Issues tab and observe 2 Open.

logicalBugs.explanation: Shared fetch actions assume all client-error responses are JSON.

rootCause.explanation: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If another user locks an issue while a non-collaborator has a comment draft open, clicking Comment shows a 'Network error SyntaxError … is not valid JSON' toast instead of saying the conversation is locked.

sourceBugs.name: Commenting on an issue that was just locked shows a raw JSON SyntaxError

reproductionPaths.expected: Submitting the stale comment explains that the conversation was locked, and the draft is kept.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking Comment showed the toast: Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON. The comment was not saved and the draft stayed; reloading removed the comment box.
reproSteps: As a repository owner, create a public repository and an issue; use a second user who is not a collaborator.
As the second user, open the issue and type a comment without submitting.
As the owner, in another session, lock the conversation on that issue.
Without reloading, click Comment as the second user.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Submitting a comment from an issue tab left open before deletion shows an internal JSON parsing exception mislabeled as a network error rather than explaining that the issue no longer exists.

sourceBugs.name: Commenting on a deleted issue shows a raw JSON SyntaxError

reproductionPaths.expected: Reject a comment on a deleted issue with readable feedback explaining that the issue is unavailable, preserving the draft.
reproductionPaths.actual: The server returns HTTP 404 with plain text Not found. The frontend parses it as JSON and displays a red Network error SyntaxError banner. The stale issue and comment draft remain visible; no comment is saved, and the Issues link still works.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue in a writable repository and open it in two tabs.
In the second tab, enter a comment without submitting it.
In the first tab, delete the issue and confirm it is gone.
Return to the stale second tab and click Comment.
Observe the raw JSON SyntaxError instead of a readable missing-issue explanation.
As a control, submit a comment on a live disposable issue and confirm it succeeds.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing reference covers a stale comment after the issue is locked. This entry covers a stale comment after the issue is deleted; both expose a parsing error in the shared comment form error handler.

guidance.scope: Covers the raw error feedback after submitting Comment or Close with Comment on an already-deleted issue. Rejection and retained draft are expected; no lost draft, persisted comment, issue restoration or navigation dead end is claimed. Add Time on a deleted issue is a separate unverified entry point.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Submitting Manually Add Time from an issue tab opened before the issue was deleted leaves the dialog open and shows a technical JSON parsing error instead of explaining that the issue no longer exists.

sourceBugs.name: Adding time to a deleted issue leaves the dialog open with a JSON parsing error

reproductionPaths.expected: The time entry is rejected with a clear message that the issue no longer exists.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Manually Add Time dialog stayed open and a red banner behind it read: Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', "Not found." is not valid JSON.
reproSteps: As the repository owner, create an issue.
Open it in a second tab, open Manually Add Time and enter a duration without submitting.
Delete the issue from the first tab.
Submit Add Time in the second tab.

logicalBugs.explanation: Repository settings accept malformed external-tracker regular expressions.

rootCause.explanation: handleSettingsPostAdvanced validates tracker URLs but assigns ExternalTrackerRegexpPattern directly to the unit configuration without compiling it, allowing invalid expressions to persist and disable reference matching.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In repository Settings, the External Issue Tracker's Regular Expression Pattern accepts a malformed pattern such as '[' and shows 'The repository settings have been updated.' Issue references then stop linking.

sourceBugs.name: External issue tracker saves an invalid regular expression and reports success

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving an invalid regular expression is rejected with a validation message instead of a success message.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Regular Expression mode and pattern '[', Update Settings showed 'The repository settings have been updated.' and the pattern was still saved after refresh. Malformed patterns such as '[', '(' or '[z-a]' make issue references like ISSUE-42, and even cross-repository PR references, render as plain text. A valid pattern links them.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, choose Use External Issue Tracker and fill in the tracker URL and URL format.
Select the Regular Expression number format and enter '[' as the pattern.
Click Update Settings, read the message, and refresh to check the saved pattern.

logicalBugs.explanation: An invalid due date is interpreted as a removal.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateIssueDeadline ignores the error returned by ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay. A five-digit year fails the Go date layout and returns zero; UpdateIssueDeadline interprets zero as delete.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Editing an issue's due date to a date with a five-digit year (for example 10000-01-01, or a typo like 20270-01-15) saves without an error but deletes the existing due date, and the timeline records it as removed.

sourceBugs.name: Entering a due date with a five-digit year silently removes the issue's due date

reproductionPaths.expected: The issue keeps its existing due date and shows a validation error for an unsupported date, rather than silently removing it.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the due date December 31, 9999, entering 01/01/10000 and saving changed the sidebar to 'No due date set' and added 'removed the due date December 31, 9999' to the timeline, with no error. The deletion persisted after refresh. Milestones reject the same input.
reproSteps: Open an issue with a due date set.
Click the due-date pencil, enter 10000-01-01 and save.
Check the due date and the timeline, then refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: Quote Reply is offered when the comment editor is unavailable.

rootCause.explanation: The quote menu remains rendered on locked discussions for readers who cannot comment. tryOnQuoteReply assumes #comment-form has a ComboMarkdownEditor and dereferences editor.value() without a missing-editor guard.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a locked issue or pull request, a user without write access has no comment box, but the ⋯ menu on the description and comments still offers Quote Reply. Clicking it does nothing visible except a JavaScript error.

sourceBugs.name: Quote Reply stays available on a locked issue for users who can't comment, and throws an error

reproductionPaths.expected: Quote Reply is hidden or disabled for users who can't comment on the locked conversation.
reproductionPaths.actual: A non-collaborator opening a locked issue saw no comment box, but the description's ⋯ menu offered Quote Reply. Clicking it did nothing and raised TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value'), shown as an error banner. The same happened on an existing comment and after a full reload.
reproSteps: As the repository owner, lock the conversation on an issue.
As a user without write access, open the issue and open the ⋯ menu on the description or a comment.
Click Quote Reply.

relatedReference.distinction: Both involve a locked issue and a user who can't comment. That entry is submitting a stale comment after the lock (raw JSON error toast); this entry is the Quote Reply menu item staying available and throwing a script error.

logicalBugs.explanation: Attachment Copy link does not escape Markdown labels.

rootCause.explanation: dropzone constructs link/image Markdown by interpolating file.name directly between brackets. Unmatched brackets break the generated syntax; HTML escaping in other media branches does not protect these Markdown labels.

reproductionPaths.explanation: For an attachment whose file name contains an unmatched square bracket (such as 'UP ] image.png' or 'y [ z.png'), the upload's Copy link inserts the name into the Markdown label without escaping, so the pasted text renders as literal Markdown instead of an image or link. Ordinary names and balanced brackets work.

sourceBugs.name: Attachment Copy link produces broken Markdown when the file name has an unmatched bracket

reproductionPaths.expected: Copy link produces Markdown that renders the image or link for any valid file name, as it does for ordinary names.
reproductionPaths.actual: Copy link for 'UP ] image.png' gave ![UP ] image.png](/attachments/…), which Preview and the posted comment showed as literal text with no image. 'y [ z.png' and the non-image 'x ] doc.txt' broke the same way, while 'plain image.png' and 'a [b] c.png' rendered correctly.
reproSteps: In an issue comment box, upload an image named 'UP ] image.png'.
Click Copy link under the upload and paste it into the comment.
Click Preview.

logicalBugs.explanation: Mentions introduced by edits do not update issue-user mention membership.

rootCause.explanation: CreateIssueComment calls FindAndUpdateIssueMentions, but UpdateComment and ChangeContent do not perform the corresponding mention membership update. Mentioning you filters rely on those rows, so edited-in mentions are absent.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When an @mention is added to an issue by editing an existing comment or the issue description, the mentioned user's issue list filter 'Mentioning you' doesn't include that issue. A mention in a newly posted comment is included.

sourceBugs.name: Mentions added by editing a comment or description don't appear under Mentioning you

reproductionPaths.expected: An issue where the user is @mentioned by an edited comment or description appears under that user's 'Mentioning you' filter, as it does for a new comment.
reproductionPaths.actual: Another user edited a plain comment to '@eval … edited ping'; eval's 'Mentioning you' showed 0 open issues for it. Posting a new comment '@eval … fresh ping' included the issue immediately. Editing an issue description to add @eval was likewise omitted.
reproSteps: As one user, post a comment without mentions on an issue, then edit it to add @<other user>.
As the mentioned user, open Issues and choose the 'Mentioning you' filter.
Compare with posting a new comment that mentions them.

logicalBugs.explanation: An inactive tracker URL still participates in browser validation.

rootCause.explanation: The advanced settings form hides the external tracker controls when Built-In is selected without disabling their URL input. Native URL validity checks still reject that hidden input and prevent the entire form submit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In repository Settings, if an invalid value is typed into the External Issue Tracker URL and the tracker is switched back to Built-In, the hidden, inactive URL field still fails browser validation. Update Settings then does nothing, so valid changes such as Time Tracking are never saved, with no visible message.

sourceBugs.name: An invalid URL left in the inactive external tracker field silently blocks saving repository settings

reproductionPaths.expected: Fields for an inactive option don't block saving, or the form shows which field is invalid; valid changes are saved.
reproductionPaths.actual: After entering 'bad-url' as the External Issue Tracker URL, switching back to Use Built-In Issue Tracker and unchecking Enable Time Tracking, Update Settings showed no success and saved nothing; Time Tracking stayed enabled. The hidden URL field still carried the browser's 'Please enter a URL.' validation error.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings, choose Use External Issue Tracker and enter 'bad-url' as its URL.
Switch back to Use Built-In Issue Tracker.
Uncheck Enable Time Tracking and click Update Settings.
Reload Settings and check Time Tracking.

relatedReference.distinction: Both involve External Issue Tracker settings. That entry is an invalid regex being accepted and saved; this entry is an invalid URL in the inactive, hidden field blocking every save.

logicalBugs.explanation: Keyword search breaks ascending creation ties in descending ID order.

rootCause.explanation: Bleve search always appends -_id to its sort. For oldest, equal created times therefore sort newest ID first, unlike the database ascending creation/id ordering.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the Issues lists, Oldest order puts issues created in the same second lowest number first, but adding a text search keyword flips them so the higher-numbered issue comes first. Keyword searches go through the search index, which breaks creation-time ties by id descending for every sort, while the unsearched list breaks Oldest ties by id ascending.

sourceBugs.name: Oldest sort reverses same-second issues once a search keyword is entered

reproductionPaths.expected: Searching keeps the selected Oldest order, so of two issues with the same creation time the lower-numbered (older) issue is still listed first.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Sort > Oldest, issue #2 was listed before #4. After searching 'release', which matches both, #4 was listed above #2. Issues created seconds apart kept the correct order.
reproSteps: Create two issues in the same second (for example through the API) whose titles share a word.
Open the Issues list and select Sort > Oldest; note the lower-numbered issue is first.
Search for the shared word.
Check which issue is listed first.

logicalBugs.explanation: Alt+Enter label exclusion loses to the dropdown keyboard handler.

rootCause.explanation: The exclusion listener is attached to the dropdown keydown, but the Fomantic keyboard path selects/activates the anchor on Enter. Its normal include navigation runs instead of the intended exclusion navigation, whereas the direct Alt+click handler sees the modifier.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The issue list's Label filter says 'Use alt + click/enter to exclude labels'. Alt+click excludes the label, but highlighting a label with the keyboard and pressing Alt+Enter includes it, so issues without that label disappear from the list.

sourceBugs.name: Alt+Enter in the Label filter includes the label instead of excluding it

reproductionPaths.expected: Pressing Alt+Enter on a highlighted label excludes it (labels=-<id>), the same as Alt+click, so issues without that label stay in the list.
reproductionPaths.actual: After typing 'documentation' in the Label filter, pressing ArrowDown and then Alt+Enter, the URL became labels=1 (included) and the list showed No results with 0 Open / 0 Closed, though unlabeled issues had been listed just before. Alt+click on the same label excluded it.
reproSteps: Open a repository's issue list with some unlabeled issues.
Open the Label filter, type a label name, and press ArrowDown to highlight it.
Press Alt+Enter.
Check whether the URL has labels=-<id> (excluded) or labels=<id> (included), and whether unlabeled issues are still listed.

logicalBugs.explanation: Cancel preserves discarded inline comment/description edits.

rootCause.explanation: cancelAndReset hides the editor and reloads attachments without resetting its text. Reopening populates rawContent only if the cached editor value is empty, so a nonempty discarded draft is reused.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After editing an issue's description (or a comment) and clicking Cancel, the saved text stays rendered, but reopening Edit without refreshing shows the cancelled draft instead of the saved text. Clicking Update from there saves the discarded draft.

sourceBugs.name: Cancelled issue description or comment edit comes back when Edit is reopened

reproductionPaths.expected: Cancel discards the edit, so reopening the editor shows the currently saved description or comment.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the saved description 'create-edit persisted baseline', the user changed it to 'create-edit discarded edit' and clicked Cancel; the page still showed the baseline, but reopening Edit showed 'create-edit discarded edit'.
reproSteps: Open an issue and choose Edit on its description (or on a comment).
Change the text and click Cancel; confirm the saved text is still shown.
Without refreshing, choose Edit again and check what the editor contains.

relatedReference.name: Canceled issue title draft reappears when editing again
relatedReference.distinction: Same symptom, but this entry is the description or comment editor (separate code), not the issue title.

logicalBugs.explanation: Timer Start and Stop are non-idempotent toggles.

rootCause.explanation: IssueStopwatch forwards both buttons to CreateOrStopIssueStopwatch without an intended target state. Requests from stale tabs toggle the current server state in the opposite direction from the button label.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If an issue's timer is stopped in one tab, clicking the still-visible Stop timer in another tab that wasn't refreshed starts a new timer instead of doing nothing. Start and Stop both send the same toggle request, which flips the timer's current state regardless of which button was clicked.

sourceBugs.name: Stop timer in an outdated tab restarts a timer already stopped elsewhere

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking Stop timer when the timer is already stopped leaves it stopped and doesn't start a new session.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the timer started in tab A and then stopped in tab B (28 seconds recorded), clicking Stop timer in the stale tab A added a new 'started working' entry to the timeline. After refresh, an active timer showed in the navigation bar.
reproSteps: Open an issue in two tabs and start its timer in tab A.
In tab B, refresh and stop the timer.
Without refreshing tab A, choose Stop timer from its Time Tracker menu.
Refresh and check whether a timer is running and whether the timeline shows a new 'started working' entry.

relatedReference.name: Start timer in an outdated tab stops a timer already running elsewhere
relatedReference.distinction: Same toggle cause, opposite direction: this entry is a stale Stop that starts a stopped timer; that entry is a stale Start that stops a running timer.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If an issue's timer is started in one tab, clicking the still-visible Start timer in another tab that wasn't refreshed stops the running timer and logs its time instead of keeping it running. Start and Stop both send the same toggle request, which flips the timer's current state regardless of which button was clicked.

sourceBugs.name: Start timer in an outdated tab stops a timer already running elsewhere

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking Start timer when the timer is already running keeps it running (or says it's already running) instead of stopping it.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the timer started in tab A, clicking Start timer in the stale tab B logged 'worked for 19 seconds' and stopped the timer. After refresh there was no active timer and Total Time Spent was 19 seconds.
reproSteps: Open an issue in two tabs with no timer running.
Start the timer in tab A.
Without refreshing tab B, choose Start timer from its Time Tracker menu.
Refresh and check whether the timer is still running or was stopped with time logged.

relatedReference.name: Stop timer in an outdated tab restarts a timer already stopped elsewhere
relatedReference.distinction: Same toggle cause, opposite direction: this entry is a stale Start that stops a running timer; that entry is a stale Stop that starts a stopped timer.

logicalBugs.explanation: The first inline edit does not insert its history indicator.

rootCause.explanation: saveAndRefresh replaces the rendered body, raw content, attachments and content-version attribute, but never refreshes the comment header containing the edited/history control. The server records the revision and reload renders it.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After saving the first inline edit of an issue comment or description, the new text appears but the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu don't appear until the page is reloaded, even though the server already recorded the revision.

sourceBugs.name: First inline edit of a comment doesn't show the edited indicator until reload

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving the first edit of a comment or issue description immediately shows the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu in the header.
reproductionPaths.actual: The edited text appears, but the header shows no '• edited' indicator or history menu; after a reload both appear with the correct history.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue and post a new comment.
Use the comment's menu > Edit, change the text, and Save.
Without reloading, check the comment header for the '• edited' indicator and history menu.
Reload the page and check the header again.

logicalBugs.explanation: Due-date changes do not refresh indexed issue deadlines.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateIssueDeadline updates the database and timeline only; indexerNotifier has no due-date change hook. Keyword searches sort the indexed DeadlineUnix from the last indexing job until another supported notification reindexes the issue.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the global Issues page with a search term, sorting by Farthest or Nearest due date uses the due date from before the last edit. Changing an issue's due date never reindexes the issue, so the search index keeps the old date until something else, such as a comment, refreshes it.

sourceBugs.name: Issue search sorted by due date keeps the old order after a due date is changed

reproductionPaths.expected: After a due date is set or changed, a search sorted by due date orders issues by their current due dates.
reproductionPaths.actual: Each row shows the new due date, but the sorted search keeps the old order. Reloading or waiting doesn't help; posting a comment on the issue fixes its position.
reproSteps: Create two issues whose titles share a unique word, and give them different due dates.
Post a comment on each issue.
