On the global Issues page, search for the shared word and sort by Farthest due date; note the order.
Change the earlier issue's due date to later than the other's, then repeat the same sorted search.
Check whether the order reflects the new date; then post a comment on that issue and search again.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (due-date updates never reindex the issue), but that entry is due dates first set on fresh issues; this entry is changing an existing due date on issues whose earlier date was already indexed.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the global Issues page with a search term, sorting by Nearest or Farthest due date ignores due dates set from the sidebar after the issues were created, so issues come back in creation order instead of date order. Setting a due date never reindexes the issue.

sourceBugs.name: Issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created
Repository issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created

reproductionPaths.expected: Issues given due dates after creation are ordered by those dates when a search is sorted by Nearest or Farthest due date.
reproductionPaths.actual: With two new issues given due dates of November 1 and December 31 from the sidebar (both saved and shown on the issues), the searched list sorted by Nearest due date put December 31 first, following creation order rather than the dates.
reproSteps: Create two issues whose titles share a unique word, without due dates.
From each issue's sidebar, set a due date, giving the older issue the earlier date.
On the global Issues page, search for the shared word and sort by Nearest due date.
Check whether the issue with the earlier due date is listed first.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date keeps the old order after a due date is changed
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (due-date updates never reindex the issue), but that entry is changing an existing due date; this entry is due dates first set on new issues, which sort as if they had none.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (setting a due date never reindexes the issue), but that entry is the global Issues page; this entry is a repository's Issues list.

logicalBugs.explanation: Attachment-only comment changes bypass optimistic concurrency.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateCommentContent increments the comment content version only when text differs. Attachment updates run separately without changing that version, allowing a stale editor to pass the version check and replace/delete newer attachments.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If an attachment is added to a comment and saved in one tab, then a comment editor opened earlier in another tab is saved (for example after removing an original attachment, or with only a text change), the newer attachment is deleted from the comment and from storage without any warning. Text-only conflicts are detected, but attachment-only changes don't update the comment's version.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a stale comment editor deletes attachments added in another tab

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving a comment editor that's out of date warns that the comment changed, as it does for text changes, and doesn't delete attachments it never showed.
reproductionPaths.actual: After tab A added and saved a file to a comment, saving the stale editor in tab B left the comment with none of the newer attachments, showed no warning, and the newer file's download link returned 404.
reproSteps: Post a comment with one attachment, then open its Edit form in two tabs.
In tab A, add a second file and save.
In tab B, remove the original attachment (or change only the text) and save.
Reload and check the comment's attachments and the second file's download link.

logicalBugs.explanation: Disabling the tracker discards its configuration.

rootCause.explanation: Advanced settings omits the Issues unit when disabled instead of retaining its options. Re-enabling constructs the unit from the default form values, restoring time tracking/dependencies rather than their previous saved values.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Turning a repository's issue tracker off and back on in Settings doesn't restore its previous options: Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies come back checked even if they were saved unchecked. The settings page greys these options out, rather than hiding them, while the feature is off, which tells the user they'll be kept and simply inactive; saving actually deletes them.

sourceBugs.name: Re-enabling the issue tracker silently turns time tracking and dependencies back on

reproductionPaths.expected: Re-enabling the issue tracker keeps the previously saved time tracking and dependency settings, as the greyed-out options shown while the tracker is disabled suggest.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies saved unchecked, disabling the issue tracker and saving, then re-enabling it and saving without touching the options, left both options checked. The Time Tracker appeared on issues again.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, uncheck Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests, and save.
Uncheck Enable Repository Issue Tracker (the issue options are greyed out, not removed) and save.
Check Enable Repository Issue Tracker again and save without changing the issue options.
Reload Settings and check the time tracking and dependency options.

relatedReference.name: Re-enabling pull requests silently turns on branch deletion and changes merge defaults
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (saving with the feature off deletes its settings while the page only greys them out), but that entry is the pull request merge settings; this entry is the issue tracker's time tracking and dependency options.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dependency timeline data is loaded without checking access to the linked issue.

rootCause.explanation: Comment.LoadDepIssueDetails loads the linked issue by ID with no actor permission filtering. The timeline renders its repository/title and conversion can expose it through the API, while the sidebar separately restricts unreadable dependencies.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When an issue in a repository is linked as depending on (or blocking) an issue in a private repository, the issue's timeline shows the private repository's name and the private issue's title to every reader, including users with no access to the private repository. The sidebar on the same page correctly hides the dependency, and the API timeline also returns the private issue.

sourceBugs.name: Dependency timeline events reveal a private issue's title to users who can't access it

reproductionPaths.expected: Readers who can't access the private repository don't see its name or the private issue's title in the timeline, as the sidebar already hides the dependency from them.
reproductionPaths.actual: Viewing the public issue as a user without access to the private repository, the sidebar said "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency", but the timeline's "added a new dependency" event showed the private repository name and issue title, linking to a 404. The API timeline returned the private issue, including its body.
reproSteps: As a user with access to both, create an issue in a private repository and an issue in a public repository.
On the public issue, add the private issue as a dependency.
Sign in as a user who can read the public repository but not the private one, and open the public issue.
Compare the sidebar's Dependencies section with the dependency event in the timeline.

logicalBugs.explanation: Disabling time tracking also prevents stopping existing timers.

rootCause.explanation: IssueStopwatch and CancelStopwatch both require CanUseTimetracker before changing state. That permission rejects a disabled unit even for an already-running timer; disabling the repository setting does not clean up those timers.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If time tracking is disabled in a repository's settings while a user's timer is running on one of its issues, the header still shows the active timer, but Stop and Discard fail with "Network error SyntaxError: … 'Not found.' is not valid JSON", and the timer can never be stopped.

sourceBugs.name: A running timer can't be stopped after time tracking is disabled for its repository

reproductionPaths.expected: After time tracking is disabled, a running timer can still be stopped or discarded, or it's stopped automatically, with no raw error.
reproductionPaths.actual: The active timer stayed in the header. Clicking Stop Timer (or Discard) showed a red network error that "Not found." isn't valid JSON, and the timer kept running.
reproSteps: In a repository with time tracking enabled, start a timer on an issue.
In the repository's settings, disable time tracking and save.
Open the active timer from the header and click Stop Timer.
Check the message and whether the timer stopped.

logicalBugs.explanation: Repeated time-log deletion is treated as an internal failure.

rootCause.explanation: GetTrackedTimeByID returns soft-deleted records. DeleteTime then receives db.ErrNotExist from deleteTime, but its post-delete error branch always returns ServerError rather than a missing/already-deleted response.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If a time log on an issue is deleted in one tab, clicking delete on the same log in another tab that hasn't been reloaded shows a red "server error: 500" instead of saying the entry no longer exists.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting an already-deleted time log from a stale tab shows a server error

reproductionPaths.expected: Deleting a time log that was already deleted shows that it no longer exists, or simply refreshes the list, without a server error.
reproductionPaths.actual: The second deletion showed a red "server error: 500" banner and the stale tab kept showing the deleted log and old total.
reproSteps: Add a manual time entry to an issue.
Open the issue in two tabs.
Delete the time entry in the first tab.
Without reloading, delete the same entry in the second tab.

logicalBugs.explanation: Inline attachment refresh bypasses embedded-image suppression.

rootCause.explanation: saveAndRefresh inserts the attachment template returned by the server directly after replacing markup. The full-page image/attachment deduplication initialization is not rerun, so an embedded attachment gets an extra thumbnail until reload.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When an issue body (or comment) already embeds one of its attached images, saving an inline edit adds a second thumbnail of that image below the attachment list until the page is reloaded.

sourceBugs.name: Saving an inline issue edit adds a duplicate thumbnail for an embedded image

reproductionPaths.expected: After saving an inline edit, an image that's already shown in the body isn't repeated below the attachments, as on a full page load.
reproductionPaths.actual: After saving the edit, a second small copy of the image appeared below the attachment rows; reloading the page removed it.
reproSteps: Create an issue with an image attachment and embed that image in the body using its link.
Use the body's menu > Edit and click Save without other changes.
Look below the attachment list, then reload and compare.

logicalBugs.explanation: Saving an empty title silently reloads the unchanged issue.

rootCause.explanation: The submit handler skips POST when the trimmed title is empty but still ignores dirty state and reloads. It never returns validation feedback for the skipped save.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Clearing an existing issue title and clicking Save closes the editor and restores the saved title without explaining that the empty value was not saved.

sourceBugs.name: Saving an empty issue title closes the editor without validation feedback

reproductionPaths.expected: An empty or whitespace-only title edit shows visible validation feedback so the user can correct it. Keeping the existing required title is valid; silently ignoring the attempted edit is the defect.
reproductionPaths.actual: Save sends no title update request, reloads the page and restores the previous title without a toast, inline message or browser validation warning. A valid nonempty replacement saves and records a title-change event.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue with a nonempty title in a writable repository.
Open the issue and click Edit beside its title.
Clear the title completely and click Save.
Observe that the editor closes and the original title returns without validation feedback.
As a control, enter a valid nonempty replacement and save; confirm the heading changes.

guidance.scope: Covers missing validation feedback after Save of an empty or whitespace-only inline issue title. Do not require an empty title to be saved, and do not describe the preserved original title as lost data.
guidance.distinction: Cancel followed by reopening a stale title draft and WIP-prefix removal failing to leave draft have separate triggers.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard ownership links lose labels omitted by request-to-view propagation.

rootCause.explanation: The dashboard template builds ownership URLs using .SelectLabels, but the user dashboard handler does not populate the repository-list SelectLabels value from the active labels query. The visible filtered result therefore cannot carry labels into those links.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the global Issues page, after filtering by a label (for example by clicking a label badge), clicking an ownership link such as Created by you drops the label filter, so issues without that label appear.

sourceBugs.name: Global Issues ownership links drop the selected label filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Switching between ownership views (Your repositories, Assigned to you, Created by you, Mentioning you) keeps the selected label filter.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a label filter applied, clicking Created by you removed the labels parameter and listed an issue without that label.
reproSteps: Create two issues you authored, one with a label and one without.
On the global Issues page, click the label's badge to filter by it.
Click Created by you.
Check whether the unlabeled issue now appears.

logicalBugs.explanation: Changing project membership leaves the indexed issue project stale.

rootCause.explanation: Project membership updates do not emit an issue-index refresh. Keyword search filters the ProjectID snapshot created by index conversion, while database-only filters use current membership; another indexing notification repairs it.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a repository's Issues list, combining a Project filter with a keyword search shows No results (or silently leaves out issues) for issues added to the project after they were created, even though each filter alone lists them. A keyword search filters by the project stored in the search index, and adding or removing an issue's project (from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action) never updates the index, so it still has the old project until something else, such as a comment or label change, reindexes the issue. Removing a project has the reverse effect with the No project filter.

sourceBugs.name: Repository issue list: filtering by a project plus a keyword search returns no results

reproductionPaths.expected: An issue in the selected project that matches the keyword is listed when the Project filter and keyword search are combined.
reproductionPaths.actual: Project = QA Board alone and the keyword alone each listed the issues, but Project = QA Board with the keyword showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed. Adding a label or comment to an issue made it appear in the combined search; untouched issues stayed hidden.
reproSteps: Create a few issues with a shared title word, and once they exist, add them to a project from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action.
On the repository's Issues list, choose that project in the Project filter and confirm the issues are listed.
Search for the shared word with the project still selected.
Check whether the issues are still listed.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date keeps the old order after a due date is changed
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (a field change that never reindexes the issue, so keyword search uses stale data), but that entry is due dates in sorted search; this entry is project membership in the Project filter.

logicalBugs.explanation: Returning from Assigned to you to All issues keeps the derived assignee.

rootCause.explanation: The list handler sets AssigneeID to the current user for type=assigned. filter_list builds every Type URL from that derived AssigneeID; changing type to all leaves assignee in the URL and keeps the restriction.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a repository's Issues list, choosing Type > Assigned to you and then Type > All issues still shows only issues assigned to you (with a search, the list stays empty), instead of returning to all matching issues.

sourceBugs.name: Switching repository issue Type from Assigned to you back to All issues keeps the assignment restriction

reproductionPaths.expected: Type > All issues lifts the restriction that Type > Assigned to you added, so the list returns to every issue matching the other filters and search.
reproductionPaths.actual: After Type > Assigned to you followed by Type > All issues, the list stayed filtered to the user's assignments and showed '0 Open' and 'No results' for a search whose unassigned matches had been listed before.
reproSteps: In a repository, create two open issues with a shared search term, one assigned to you and one unassigned.
Open the repository Issues list and search the shared term; both issues appear.
Choose Type > Assigned to you.
Choose Type > All issues and check whether the unassigned issue comes back.

relatedReference.distinction: Same implicit assignment carried over from a previous Type choice. That entry is the repository Pull Requests list; this entry is the repository Issues list.

otherRelatedReference.distinction: Same retained Assigned to you restriction on a milestone's issue list.

guidance.scope: Only the Type control: going from Type > Assigned to you to Type > All issues (or another Type) keeps the assignment restriction that the earlier Type choice added. This is not a toggle of an explicit filter. If the user also selected themselves in the Assignee filter, keeping that explicit Assignee filter after changing Type is expected and is not this bug.

logicalBugs.explanation: Removing an unreadable dependency submits its direction backwards and gets an empty response.

rootCause.explanation: Locked Depends-on rows emit dependency-type blocking instead of blockedBy. RemoveDependency attempts to delete the reversed edge; ErrDependencyNotExists sets a flash error then returns without a redirect/body, producing a blank 200 page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an issue that depends on an issue the user can't read, the sidebar shows a lock and says the user can still remove the dependency. Confirming Remove opens a completely blank page, and the dependency is not removed.

sourceBugs.name: Removing a dependency on an issue you can't read opens a blank page and keeps the dependency

reproductionPaths.expected: Confirming Remove deletes the dependency and returns to the issue, as it does for dependencies the user can read.
reproductionPaths.actual: After confirming Remove on the locked 'Depends on' dependency, the browser landed on the dependency delete URL showing an empty document with no message or controls. Reopening the issue showed the dependency still in place and no error.
reproSteps: Make an issue in one repository depend on an issue in a private repository.
Sign in as a user who can write to the first repository but can't read the private one, and open the first issue.
In the sidebar, the dependency shows a lock with the tooltip that you can remove it; click its remove icon and confirm.
Check the page shown and whether the dependency was removed.

guidance.scope: Removing a locked (unreadable) dependency from an issue's sidebar leads to a blank page, or the dependency is not removed.

logicalBugs.explanation: Inline edit errors unconditionally parse JSON before status handling.

rootCause.explanation: saveAndRefresh calls response.json() before checking HTTP status and only renders structured errorMessage for 400. A plain-text 404 from UpdateCommentContent for a deleted comment throws into the raw exception toast.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If a comment is deleted (for example from another tab) while its inline editor is open, clicking Save shows a technical error banner, 'Failed to save the content: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', "Not found." is not valid JSON', instead of explaining that the comment no longer exists. The editor closes and the old comment text is shown.

sourceBugs.name: Saving an edit to a comment deleted in another tab shows a raw JSON SyntaxError

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving an edit to a comment that no longer exists shows a readable message that the comment was deleted, as the editor does for a version conflict.
reproductionPaths.actual: The server returned HTTP 404 with plain text 'Not found.', and the page showed the raw SyntaxError banner, hid the editor and displayed the stale comment card. Reopening Edit still contained the pending text.
reproSteps: Open an issue with a comment you can edit, and open the same issue in a second tab.
In the first tab, click Edit on the comment and change its text without saving.
In the second tab, delete that comment.
In the first tab, click Save and read the error shown.

relatedReference.name: Commenting on a deleted issue shows a raw JSON SyntaxError
relatedReference.distinction: Same raw JSON SyntaxError from a plain-text 404. That entry is posting a new comment on a deleted issue; this entry is saving an inline edit to a comment that was deleted.

guidance.scope: Saving an inline comment (or description) edit after the comment was deleted elsewhere shows a raw JSON parsing error. Claims that the pending edit text is lost are not part of this bug: reopening Edit keeps it.

logicalBugs.explanation: Tracker validation redirects discard other submitted tracker values.

rootCause.explanation: handleSettingsPostAdvanced handles invalid tracker URLs/formats by flashing an error and redirecting to settings. That GET renders persisted unit settings instead of the submitted draft, resetting other entered values.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, submitting the external issue tracker with an invalid URL shows the error, but the form reloads with Built-In issue tracker selected, the URL Format empty and no number style chosen, discarding everything the user entered.

sourceBugs.name: External issue tracker validation error discards the other entered tracker settings

reproductionPaths.expected: After a validation error, the form keeps the entered tracker type, URL format and number style so only the rejected field needs fixing.
reproductionPaths.actual: Choosing External Issue Tracker with an invalid tracker URL, a URL format and Alphanumeric showed 'The external issue tracker URL is not a valid URL.' The reloaded form showed Built-In selected, an empty URL Format and no style selected; nothing was saved. The same inputs with a valid URL saved and persisted.
reproSteps: Open a repository's Settings and go to Advanced Settings.
Select External Issue Tracker, enter an invalid tracker URL, a URL format and choose Alphanumeric.
Click Update Settings.
Check the tracker type, URL format and number style shown with the error.

relatedReference.distinction: Same validation error discarding unsaved settings edits. That entry is the Basic Settings repository name; this entry is the Advanced Settings external issue tracker.

otherRelatedReference.distinction: Same validation-wipes-the-draft pattern on the branch protection form.

guidance.scope: Advanced Settings external issue tracker (or URL format) validation errors resetting the entered tracker type, URL format or number style.
